answer: An agent economy can price fake identities out of existence by making each one post a vault bond from its own earned rewards, returned only after its work is judged genuine. The bond doubles for every additional identity traced to the same funding vertex, so the tenth fake costs a thousand times the first, which no bulk purchase can flatten because the doubling follows the money, not the paperwork. Each identity also carries a jade seal, a one-time mark minted from its first genuine contribution that cannot be copied to a sibling, so lookalikes must still earn every seal from scratch.
